findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancellation aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
findings.body: The entire cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and each SendGrid request is awaited inside it. If cancelling one reminder fails (for example an invalid or already-cancelled batch_id), the exception exits the loop, the remaining reminders in the next-hour window are never sent a cancellation request, and the Prisma delete operations already queued in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited (they are lazy Prisma promises), so even successfully-cancelled reminders keep their rows. Those uncancelled SendGrid emails will still be delivered for cancelled/rescheduled bookings. Each reminder needs its own error handling so one failure does not block the rest.

findings.title: Last-minute cancellations are deleted without ever cancelling the SendGrid email
findings.body: Deferred cancellation only happens when the cron job runs and finds cancelled=true with scheduledDate within the next hour, but at the top of the same handler all EMAIL workflowReminders with scheduledDate <= now are deleted unconditionally before the cancellation block runs. If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run before its reminder's send time (the PR states the cron runs every 15 minutes), the next run can cross the scheduledDate, delete the DB row first, and never issue the SendGrid cancel for that batch; SendGrid has already dispatched the email. The reminder for a just-cancelled booking is therefore still sent in this window, and the row deletion removes any chance of a later retry.

findings.title: immediateDelete path leaves the reminder row active with no retry if SendGrid fails
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder issues the SendGrid cancel request and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. The reschedule caller in handleNewBooking.ts relies on this path and does not delete the old booking's reminders via cascade, so the old row remains scheduled=true/cancelled=null; the cron job only retries rows with cancelled=true, so if the SendGrid request throws (the error is only logged inside this function) nothing ever retries the cancellation and the old booking's reminder email is still sent. It also leaves stale scheduled reminder rows attached to the superseded booking until their scheduledDate passes.

findings.title: Reminder cancellations are fired without awaiting persistence of the cancelled flag
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach(...) calls the async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and discards the returned promises. The handler then deletes attendees/references, sends cancellation emails and returns 200 without guaranteeing the prisma update that sets cancelled=true (or the SMS/Twilio cancellation and row deletion) has completed. In a serverless/short-lived invocation the process can finish or be frozen before the update lands, leaving the reminder active for the cron/SendGrid to send; the same un-awaited pattern in the try/catch in handleNewBooking.ts also means that try/catch can never observe failures. These promises should be collected and awaited (e.g. Promise.all) before responding.
